findings.title: Architecture Analysis of ai-repo-analyser Repository
findings.description: The repository `ai-repo-analyser` is a web application that integrates both frontend and backend components. The architecture appears to be a combination of microservices and layered architectures, with clear separation between the frontend and backend.

findings.title: Frontend
findings.description: The frontend uses React (version 18+) as its framework. The main entry point is `src/main.tsx`. It includes an `App` component that renders various sections like features and footer.

findings.title: Backend
findings.description: The backend uses Express.js as its framework. The main entry point is `server/index.js`. It includes endpoints for authentication (`/api/auth/github`), repository analysis (`/api/analyze`), and user information (`/api/user`).

findings.title: Layered Architecture
findings.description: The backend is structured in a layered manner with clear separation of concerns. It includes middleware, authentication, repository analysis, database interaction, and error handling.

findings.title: Microservices Architecture
findings.description: The application can be considered a microservice with distinct services (authentication, repository analysis) that interact through APIs. The frontend communicates with the backend via RESTful API endpoints.

findings.title: Frontend-Backend Interaction
findings.description: The frontend makes HTTP requests to the backend for fetching repositories, analyzing them, and handling user sessions. This interaction is facilitated through well-defined API endpoints provided by the backend.

findings.title: Conclusion
findings.description: The `ai-repo-analyser` repository follows a layered architecture with clear separation between the frontend and backend components. The use of Express.js on the backend and React on the frontend ensures modularity and maintainability. Additionally, the implementation of microservices principles through distinct services interacting via APIs enhances scalability and flexibility.

findings.title: Recommendations
findings.description: Suggestions include ensuring each service is well-encapsulated, implementing unit tests for both frontend and backend components, and enhancing security measures such as input validation, secure session management, and proper handling of sensitive data.

findings.title: Summary
findings.description: The `ai-repo-analyser` repository is well-structured with a clear separation between the frontend and backend. The use of microservices principles and layered architecture enhances maintainability and scalability. Further improvements can be made in code organization, testing, and security to ensure robustness and reliability.

installation_steps: Ensure you have Node.js installed on your system. You can download it from the official Node.js website.
Clone the repository to your local machine using `git clone <repository-url>`.

environment_variables.name: Set up the required environment variables in a `.env` file at the root of your project directory. Here are the necessary variables:
- GEMINI_API_KEY: Your API key for Gemini service (default value: none).
- MONGO_URI: MongoDB connection URI (default value: none).
- PORT: The port number on which the server will run (default value: environment variable `PORT`).
- FRONTEND_URL: URL of your frontend application (default value: environment variable `FRONTEND_URL`).
- GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: Client ID for GitHub OAuth integration (default value: environment variable `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`).
- GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: Client secret for GitHub OAuth integration (default value: environment variable `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`)

run_commands.command: Navigate to the project directory in your terminal.
Run `npm install` or `yarn install` to install all dependencies.
Start the backend server with `npm run dev` or `yarn dev`. This command will start both the frontend and backend if they are integrated, otherwise it will only start the backend.

testing_commands: To run tests, use `npm test` or `yarn test` in your terminal. Ensure that all tests pass before proceeding.
